title_candidates: Try AstaBrief, then check its citations
Asta turns a research question into a cited report
summary: Ai2's Asta can turn a focused research question into a cited report in minutes, but readers should check the sources and understand the data-consent trade-off.

primary_source.title: Open-sourcing AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model in Asta
primary_source.author: Kyle Wiggers, Ai2Comms
key_facts: AstaBrief 8B converts a research question plus retrieved scientific-literature excerpts into a report with citations.
Ai2 built the model from Qwen3-8B and trained it with supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization.
The model powers Asta's Fast mode, while the weights, training data, and an example PDF-to-report workflow are publicly available.
Ai2 reports that its full Fast-mode pipeline averaged 51.1 seconds per report, compared with 178.5 seconds for its Claude-powered Thinking mode.
Ai2 says the strongest quality gains in its training experiments came from filtering synthetic reports with weak citation density.
Open weights let institutions run AstaBrief on their own infrastructure, including behind a firewall for sensitive or unpublished work.
Ai2 cautions that most training and evaluation occurred in 2025, its full evaluation was not rerun against current frontier models, and its human comparison covered 14 questions.

supporting_sources.title: AstaBrief 8B model card
key_facts: The official model card describes the Apache-2.0 checkpoint, its Qwen3-8B base, cited-report purpose, downloadable weights, and limitations.

supporting_sources.title: Asta
key_facts: The hosted Asta interface offers Generate a report with Fast and Thinking modes; signing in is presented as a way to save work rather than a requirement to reach the composer.
During editorial testing on October 6, the first-use acceptance button stayed disabled until the separate public-dataset consent box was selected, despite that choice being described as optional.

supporting_sources.title: Ai2 Privacy Policy
key_facts: Ai2 says prompts and search queries entered in its demonstrations may be collected and used to improve services and support research or educational programs.
The hosted workflow should not be used for personal, confidential, proprietary, sensitive, or unpublished material.

prerequisites: A modern browser with JavaScript enabled
A focused scientific question containing no sensitive, confidential, proprietary, or unpublished information

steps.instruction: Open [Asta](https://asta.allen.ai/) and leave Generate a report selected; sign-in is only needed if you want to save work.
Open the mode menu, choose Fast mode, and confirm that the button now reads Fast mode.
Enter a narrow public-information question with clear scope, such as asking how two named research ideas differ, then select Send.
Read the first-use data-consent dialog before continuing. During our test, Accept & Use Asta stayed disabled until the public-dataset opt-in was checked; stop if that sharing is not acceptable.

When the report appears, open at least two citations and confirm that each paper supports the nearby claim without expanding its sample, setting, causation, or certainty. Treat the report as a starting synthesis, not a final authority.

references.title: Open-sourcing AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model in Asta
references.author: Kyle Wiggers, Ai2Comms

risk_flags: The hosted first-use consent behavior was observed on 2026-10-06 and may change; readers should rely on the dialog they see.
Citations are not an accuracy guarantee; the guide requires opening and checking at least two sources.
The hosted workflow is unsuitable for sensitive or unpublished material; local deployment is a separate technical path.
Vendor timing and quality comparisons are attributed to Ai2 and are not independent current-model benchmarks.
